messages.content: Write a recap post about what a team learned at an industry conference. Around 250 words.

output:

**What we took home from [Conference]**

Four of us went. We came back arguing about one talk, which is usually the sign a conference paid for itself.

The talk was [Speaker]'s, on incident review. Her argument: most postmortems are written for a reader who never shows up. She'd pulled two years of her team's docs and found the median one got read twice — once by the author, once by whoever approved it. Then it sat in the wiki. Her fix is small and slightly annoying. Every postmortem has to name a specific runbook, alert, or doc it changes. No change, no postmortem.

We don't agree on whether that's too strict. [Name] thinks it kills the "we got lucky" writeups that produce no action but still teach you something, which is a fair objection. We're going to try it for a quarter anyway and see what we lose.

Two other things stuck.

The hallway mood on vector databases has cooled since last year. Nobody was selling us one. Three separate people said some version of "we moved that back into Postgres," unprompted.

And the deployment track was quieter and more useful than the AI track — fewer people, better questions. If you go next year, skip the keynote hall.

Slides are in the shared drive. If you want the long version of the postmortem argument, come find me. I'd rather talk it through than write it up.
